12: /// ## What it does
13: /// Checks for commented-out Python code.
14: ///
15: /// ## Why is this bad?
16: /// Commented-out code is dead code, and is often included inadvertently.
17: /// It should be removed.
18: ///
19: /// ## Known problems
20: /// Prone to false positives when checking comments that resemble Python code,
21: /// but are not actually Python code ([#4845]).
22: ///
23: /// ## Example
24: /// ```python
25: /// # print("Hello, world!")
26: /// ```
27: ///
28: /// ## Options
29: /// - `lint.task-tags`
30: ///
31: /// [#4845]: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/4845
32: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
33: pub(crate) struct CommentedOutCode;

35: impl Violation for CommentedOutCode {
36:     const FIX_AVAILABILITY: FixAvailability = FixAvailability::None;
37: 
38:     #[derive_message_formats]
39:     fn message(&self) -> String {
40:         "Found commented-out code".to_string()
41:     }
42: 
43:     fn fix_title(&self) -> Option<String> {
44:         Some("Remove commented-out code".to_string())
45:     }
46: }

48: /// ERA001
49: pub(crate) fn commented_out_code(
50:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
51:     locator: &Locator,
52:     comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
53:     settings: &LinterSettings,
54: ) {
55:     let mut comments = comment_ranges.into_iter().peekable();
56:     // Iterate over all comments in the document.
57:     while let Some(range) = comments.next() {
58:         let line = locator.line_str(range.start());
59: 
60:         if is_script_tag_start(line) {
61:             if skip_script_comments(range, &mut comments, locator) {
62:                 continue;
63:             }
64:         }
65: 
66:         // Verify that the comment is on its own line, and that it contains code.
67:         if is_own_line_comment(line) && comment_contains_code(line, &settings.task_tags[..]) {
68:             let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(CommentedOutCode, range);
69:             diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::display_only_edit(Edit::range_deletion(
70:                 locator.full_lines_range(range),
71:             )));
72:             diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
73:         }
74:     }
75: }

77: /// Parses the rest of a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)

79: /// the script comment is invalid.
80: ///
81: /// Returns `true` if it is a valid script comment.
82: fn skip_script_comments<I>(
83:     script_start: TextRange,
84:     comments: &mut std::iter::Peekable<I>,
85:     locator: &Locator,
86: ) -> bool
87: where
88:     I: Iterator<Item = TextRange>,
89: {

91:     let opener = locator.line_str(script_start.start());
92:     let opener_is_script;
93:     if opener.is_empty() {
94:         opener_is_script = false;
95:     } else {
96:         let opener_bytes = opener.as_bytes();
97:         if opener_bytes.len() != 12 {
98:             opener_is_script = false;
99:         } else if opener_bytes[0] != b'#' {
100:             opener_is_script = false;
101:         } else if opener_bytes[1] != b' ' {
102:             opener_is_script = false;
103:         } else if opener_bytes[2] != b'/' {
104:             opener_is_script = false;
105:         } else if opener_bytes[3] != b'/' {
106:             opener_is_script = false;
107:         } else if opener_bytes[4] != b'/' {
108:             opener_is_script = false;
109:         } else if opener_bytes[5] != b' ' {
110:             opener_is_script = false;
111:         } else if opener_bytes[6] != b's' {
112:             opener_is_script = false;
113:         } else if opener_bytes[7] != b'c' {
114:             opener_is_script = false;
115:         } else if opener_bytes[8] != b'r' {
116:             opener_is_script = false;
117:         } else if opener_bytes[9] != b'i' {
118:             opener_is_script = false;
119:         } else if opener_bytes[10] != b'p' {
120:             opener_is_script = false;
121:         } else if opener_bytes[11] != b't' {
122:             opener_is_script = false;
123:         } else {
124:             opener_is_script = true;
125:         }
126:     }
127:     if !opener_is_script {
128:         return false;
129:     }
130: 
131:     let start_index = usize::from(script_start.end());
132:     let source_len = source.len();
133:     let source_bytes = source.as_bytes();
134:     let mut line_end = TextSize::try_from(source_len).unwrap_or_default();
135:     if start_index < source_len {
136:         let mut cursor = start_index;
137:         let mut found_line_break = false;
138:         while cursor < source_len {
139:             let current = source_bytes[cursor];
140:             if current == b'\n' {
141:                 let next_index = cursor + 1;
142:                 if let Ok(converted) = TextSize::try_from(next_index) {
143:                     line_end = converted;
144:                     found_line_break = true;
145:                 }
146:                 break;
147:             } else if current == b'\r' {
148:                 if cursor + 1 < source_len {
149:                     if source_bytes[cursor + 1] == b'\n' {
150:                         let next_index = cursor + 2;
151:                         if let Ok(converted) = TextSize::try_from(next_index) {
152:                             line_end = converted;
153:                             found_line_break = true;
154:                         }
155:                         break;
156:                     }
157:                     let next_index = cursor + 1;
158:                     if let Ok(converted) = TextSize::try_from(next_index) {
159:                         line_end = converted;
160:                         found_line_break = true;
161:                     }
162:                     break;
163:                 }
164:                 let next_index = cursor + 1;
165:                 if let Ok(converted) = TextSize::try_from(next_index) {
166:                     line_end = converted;
167:                     found_line_break = true;
168:                 }
169:                 break;
170:             } else {
171:                 cursor += 1;
172:             }
173:         }
174:         if !found_line_break {
175:             if let Ok(converted) = TextSize::try_from(source_len) {
176:                 line_end = converted;
177:             }
178:         }
179:     } else if source_len == 0 {
180:         line_end = TextSize::from(0);
181:     }

183:     let mut offset = line_end;
184:     let mut end_offset: Option<TextSize> = None;
185: 
186:     loop {
187:         let index = usize::from(offset);
188:         if index >= source_len {
189:             break;
190:         }
191:         let rest = &source[index..];
192:         if rest.is_empty() {
193:             break;
194:         }

196:         let rest_bytes = rest.as_bytes();
197:         let mut newline_at = None;
198:         let mut newline_width = 0usize;
199:         let mut search = 0usize;
200:         while search < rest_bytes.len() {
201:             let byte = rest_bytes[search];
202:             if byte == b'\n' {

204:                 newline_width = 1;
205:                 break;
206:             }
207:             if byte == b'\r' {
208:                 if search + 1 < rest_bytes.len() {
209:                     if rest_bytes[search + 1] == b'\n' {
210:                         newline_at = Some(search);
211:                         newline_width = 2;
212:                         break;
213:                     }
214:                     newline_at = Some(search);
215:                     newline_width = 1;
216:                     break;
217:                 }
218:                 newline_at = Some(search);
219:                 newline_width = 1;
220:                 break;
221:             }
222:             search += 1;
223:         }
224: 
225:         let (line_text, line_full_end, next_offset) = if let Some(position) = newline_at {
226:             let full_width = position + newline_width;

255:                 } else if first == '\t' {
256:                     valid_content = None;
257:                 } else {
258:                     valid_content = None;
259:                 }

261:                 valid_content = None;
262:             }
263:         }

265:         let Some(content) = valid_content else {

267:         };

269:         let mut is_terminator = false;

272:             if let Some(first_slash) = slashes.next() {
273:                 if first_slash == '/' {
274:                     if let Some(second_slash) = slashes.next() {
275:                         if second_slash == '/' {
276:                             if let Some(third_slash) = slashes.next() {
277:                                 if third_slash == '/' && slashes.next().is_none() {
278:                                     is_terminator = true;
279:                                 }
280:                             }
281:                         }
282:                     }
283:                 }
284:             }
285:         }
286: 
287:         if is_terminator {
288:             let lookahead_index = usize::from(next_offset);
289:             let mut lookahead_is_embedded_line = false;
290:             let mut lookahead_end = next_offset;
291:             if lookahead_index < source_len && !source[lookahead_index..].is_empty() {
292:                 let lookahead_rest = &source[lookahead_index..];
293:                 let lookahead_bytes = lookahead_rest.as_bytes();
294:                 let mut look_nl_at = None;
295:                 let mut look_nl_width = 0usize;
296:                 let mut look_search = 0usize;
297:                 while look_search < lookahead_bytes.len() {
298:                     let look_byte = lookahead_bytes[look_search];
299:                     if look_byte == b'\n' {
300:                         look_nl_at = Some(look_search);
301:                         look_nl_width = 1;
302:                         break;
303:                     }
304:                     if look_byte == b'\r' {
305:                         if look_search + 1 < lookahead_bytes.len() {
306:                             if lookahead_bytes[look_search + 1] == b'\n' {
307:                                 look_nl_at = Some(look_search);
308:                                 look_nl_width = 2;
309:                                 break;
310:                             }
311:                             look_nl_at = Some(look_search);
312:                             look_nl_width = 1;
313:                             break;
314:                         }
315:                         look_nl_at = Some(look_search);
316:                         look_nl_width = 1;
317:                         break;
318:                     }

322:                 let (look_text, look_full_end) = if let Some(position) = look_nl_at {
323:                     let full_width = position + look_nl_width;
324:                     let text = &lookahead_rest[..position];
325:                     let full_end = next_offset + TextSize::try_from(full_width).unwrap_or_default();
326:                     (text, full_end)

342:                                 lookahead_is_embedded_line = true;

346:                         } else if look_first == '\t' {

392: /// Returns `true` if line contains an own-line comment.
393: fn is_own_line_comment(line: &str) -> bool {
394:     for char in line.chars() {
395:         if char == '#' {
396:             return true;
397:         }
398:         if !char.is_whitespace() {
399:             return false;
400:         }
401:     }
402:     unreachable!("Comment should contain '#' character")
403: }

part.text:
All 2219 tests pass. The fix is complete:

**Root cause:** `skip_script_comments` in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/eradicate/rules/commented_out_code.rs` used a lookahead heuristic after finding a `# ///` terminator: if the next line was any comment line, it treated the terminator as content and kept scanning for another terminator. In the issue's example, the trailing `#` / `# Bla bla bla` lines after `# ///` triggered this, so no second terminator was ever found, the block was treated as unclosed, and the comments inside were flagged as ERA001.

**Fix:** Replaced the convoluted byte-scanning logic with a clean line-based scan (matching upstream ruff): iterate lines via `UniversalNewlineIterator`, parse each line with a new `script_line_content` helper (accepts `#` or `# ` prefixed lines, stops at any non-comment line), and record the **last** `///` line as the block end. A trailing comment line after the terminator no longer invalidates it, while the multi-line-string edge case (`script_comment_end_precedence`) still resolves to the final `# ///`.

Verified: the exact issue reproduction passes `ruff check --select ERA001`, and all `ruff_linter` tests (2219) pass, including the pre-existing ERA001 fixture case added for this issue.
